RAN#106 approved WI for Ambient IoT in [1]. One of the objectives for RAN2 is listed as follows: In RAN2#129 [2], the following agreements were made: To allow further discussion of the FFD items, RAN2#129 allocated an email discussion [3]: The report from this email discussion makes a number of proposals which were discussed during RAN2#129bis. Some proposals relating to the expected behaviour of the device when it receives a new service request while processing an earlier one are quoted below: During RAN2#129bis [4[, an offline discussion [5] was held to determine whether to choose from proposal 1: Option (a): Ignore all new requests and R2D messages addressed to itself but not associated with the ongoing procedure or: Option (b): Terminate the ongoing procedure and respond to the latest request No conclusion was reached and the decision was deferred to the present meeting. In this contribution we revisit the issue. A key issue is that there is no clear mechanism by which a device can determine that a service request has completed. If it is addressed by a new service request, that is, it receives a new service request with a valid address, is it safe for the device to assume that the current service request has been terminated and to follow the new service request?

hitectures should be derived after the requirements are clearly defined. Discussing the termination point without a clear consensus on "who needs the data (Consumer)" and "timeliness/periodicity requirements (QoS)" may lead to premature or suboptimal decisions (e.g., data volume class and periodicity assumptions). Therefore, the "Requirement Phase" should be preferably separated from the "Architecture Phase". We should first prioritize agreeing on the Consumer and QoS for each agreed Data Type. The decision on selecting the appropriate termination point and RAN Decodability should be deferred until these requirements are stable. Based on the discussion, the following approach is observed: The determination of the termination point depends on the definition of Consumer and QoS requirements, while RAN Decodability primarily depends on the definition of Consumer. In the current phase, the study should primarily focus on defining the Consumer and QoS for each data type to enable the selection of the appropriate termination point. In this Requirement Phase, the expected output is a common understanding per data type on (a) primary consumer(s), (b) indicative latency category/periodicity, and (c) rough data volume class, enabling an informed decision on termination point and RAN decodability.

Athens, Greece, 13–17 February 2017 Agenda item: 10.6 Document for: Discussion & Decision Introduction Rel-15 scope discussion may take significant time. We suggest that NR RAN2 scope and planning for Rel-15 is pre-discussed in RAN2, such that it can be better determined what is a minimal consensus scope, and which are the scope points that require further discussion. The following kind of NR related items are assumed to be covered in Rel-15 WI for NR Phase 1 and LTE parts of NR-LTE interworking in Phase 1 SI(s) for NR Phase 2 Phase 1 vs Phase 2 With an aggressive schedule for NR Standardization in Phase 1, any non-essential aspect of NR should be deemed as a potential candidate for being deferred to Phase 2. We therefore recommend RAN2 to identify the essential aspects of NR (without which NR cannot work i.e. without which applicable requirements in TR38.913 cannot be met), distinctively from the non-essential ones (e.g. nice-to-have). The latter could be discussed on a case-by-case basis i.e. whether to be covered in Phase 1 or to be deferred to Phase 2. In addition, items that were put on hold for consideration at RAN#75/Mar2017 (see RP-161914) are as such candidates for Phase 2 – we recommend discussions as to which should be considered for Phase 2 (study) or not. (RP-161914: Waveforms above 40GHz, mMTC, [Flexible duplex of paired spectrum], Interworking with non-3GPP systems, Wireless relay, Satellite communication, Air-to-ground and light air craft communications, Extreme long distance coverage, Sidelink, V2V and V2X, Multimedia Broadcast/Multicast Service, Shared spectrum and unlicensed spectrum, [Location/positioning functionality], Public warning/emergency alert, New SON functionality) Further Candidates for postponement to Phase 2 We suggest it could be discussed which of the following items are possible candidates for postponement, NR-NR Dual Conn – This seems like a lower priority item Intra-NR CA – Assuming that the initial deployments will have wide single carrier bandwidth, we could postpone Carrier aggregation. eLTE, i.e. LTE CP connected to NG-Core, scen 5 and 7/7a in RP-161266 - For eLTE, there will need to be discussions on each new/modified NAS feature that impact AS, how and to what extent it is implemented at AS, thus the effort is not neligible. eLTE can be developed smoother in a second phase where there is a stable baseline of specified features in NR. Assume stationary UEs for HF Stand-Alone – If we assume stationary UEs for HF stand-alone, the RRM functions and Paging do not need to be optimized for mobile UEs. RRC_Inactive – It is better to have an ambition level that can also cover m2m cases, to avoid a future CIOT optimizations with architecture impacts, than to do something quick with marginal efficiency enhancements compared to Connected / Idle.

According to the discussion during RAN2#115-e meeting, there are many potential issues to be discussed and determined for positioning in RRC_INACTIVE state. In the subsequent sections, we provide our views on DL positioning and UL/UL+DL positioning, respectively. In previous meetings, there were some discussions on support type of location services. In summary, there are three options as follows for INACTIVE positioning. Option1: Support only deferred MT-LR Option2: Support both deferred MT-LR and MO-LR Option3: Ask SA2 to make the decision When UE is in SDT active period, it has been agreed the network can send DL LCS, LPP message and RRC message to the UE. That is, after the UE initiated data transmission using UL SDT probably for some traffics other than positioning service, network can trigger location service during SDT active period. There is no reason to preclude this case. Thus, MT-LR, NI-LR and deferred MT-LR can be supported. In our view, from RAN2 perspective, both all location service types should be specified as what we did in Rel-16. From SA2 perspective, we don’t think there is a necessity for enhancement since RRC state is transparent to LMF. Proposal 1: Support all location service types from RAN2 perspective including MT-LR, MO-LR, NI-LR and deferred MT-LR.

In summary, there are three options as follows for INACTIVE positioning. Option1: Support only deferred MT-LR Option2: Support both deferred MT-LR and MO-LR Option3: Ask SA2 to make the decision When UE is in SDT active period, it has been agreed the network can send DL LCS, LPP message and RRC message to the UE. That is, after the UE initiated data transmission using UL SDT probably for some traffics other than positioning service, network can trigger location service during SDT active period. There is no reason to preclude this case. Thus, MT-LR, NI-LR and deferred MT-LR can be supported. In our view, from RAN2 perspective, both all location service types should be specified as what we did in Rel-16. From SA2 perspective, we don’t think there is a necessity for enhancement since RRC state is transparent to LMF. Proposal 1: Support all location service types from RAN2 perspective including MT-LR, MO-LR, NI-LR and deferred MT-LR.

General RAN2 110 electronic has full decision power, i.e. full decision power to make agreements and approvals according to RAN WG2 terms of reference, without any need to ratify decisions at a later RAN2 or other meeting. Note that Contributions should be reserved for more complicated issued and minor issues are expected to be resolved in RRC email discussions or by CR rapporteur without any tdoc.
